leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members explicitly include targeted protein degradation (B014) in their round-1 configuration, one more than the five needed for a majority, but they do not share a configuration. Aili, Aqvist and Sparr name Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli; Linke and Zou name Crews, Deshaies and Handa; Chabes names only Crews and Deshaies, for the conception and first demonstration of PROTACs, and pairs this with a second part. All six use the event-driven, induced-proximity framing. They differ on whether the citation covers PROTACs only (Chabes, and by construction the Ciulli trios) or also the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism (Linke, Zou), so agreement on the topic is not yet agreement on a citation.

Chabes alone prefers a two-part prize: B014 for Crews and Deshaies (PROTACs) and B042 for David R. Liu alone (base editing). Chabes moved away from the three-person base-editing unit of his opening ballot to Liu alone, which leaves a seat for Crews and Deshaies and avoids the Komor/Gaudelli credit question. Chabes also raises whether two chemical-biology parts in one year is acceptable.

Somfai alone prefers a two-part prize: B057 (palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling) for Buchwald and Hartwig, and B042 for Liu alone. Somfai acknowledges that B057 had weak opening support (four members ranked it, three of them sixth to eighth) and that it may look incremental after the 2010 cross-coupling prize. B042 is shared with Chabes's configuration, but the two do not pair it with the same first part.

Brzezinski alone prefers B025 (long-range electron transfer through proteins) for Gray and Winkler, valuing a stated physical principle over a tool or modality. Brzezinski concedes that B025 had one first-place vote and little other opening support, that it builds on Marcus theory (recognised in 1992), and that it overlaps with his own research area. Brzezinski lists B014 and B042 as alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: B014 is the only shortlisted achievement that every member ranked at opening, and six of eight members now place it in their preferred configuration; the other two list it as an alternative (Brzezinski, Somfai).

All members who support B014 describe it as a shift from occupancy-driven to event-driven pharmacology through induced proximity (a ternary complex recruiting the ubiquitin-proteasome system), confirmed independently over about two decades and across many ligases.

B042 (base editing) is the most common second choice: Chabes and Somfai prefer it as a part, and Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Sparr and Zou list it as an alternative. Its chemistry is accepted as a defined deaminase reaction on a Cas-bound single-stranded DNA window.
Members who favour B014 name Crews and Deshaies as the conceptual and first-demonstration core, and no member of the six proposes a configuration without both of them.
The six B014 supporters each say clinical proof for heterobifunctional degraders is still maturing, and all eight members report no conflict that requires recusal.
scientific_disputes: Whether one citation can credibly cover both PROTACs (designed bifunctional molecules) and molecular glues (cereblon as the thalidomide target), or whether these are two discoveries. Linke and Zou regard them as one principle; Chabes, Aqvist and Sparr treat the glue lineage as separate and unrecognised in a Ciulli-based trio.
Whether base editing (B042) is a distinct chemical invention or an application of the genome-targeting platform recognised in 2020 (raised by Aili, Chabes, Linke, Somfai).
Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B057) adds a new capability beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize (Somfai's own reservation; Linke asked the same).

Whether the Gray-Winkler results on protein electron transfer (B025) add to Marcus theory and Dutton's work on natural proteins, and what weight a stated physical mechanism should carry against a modality that has reached patients (Brzezinski).

Sparr's own opening first choice, phase separation (B045), is not in any preferred configuration; she says that whether condensates are equilibrium phenomena is still contested and she does not think it can carry the prize this year.
attribution_disputes: The third seat in B014: Ciulli (VHL ligands, first fully small-molecule VHL-based degraders, ternary-complex structure; Aili, Aqvist, Sparr) versus Handa (identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target; Linke, Zou). Ciulli would give a PROTAC-centred prize and Handa would add the glue arm. Chabes would leave the third seat for B042.

Sakamoto and Kim, co-authors of the 2001 PROTAC paper, are in no member's configuration. Ito (with Handa), Gray and the other credited names are also left out of all six, and Aili asks specifically about priority and credit in the 2001 work.

For B042, whether Liu alone or the Liu, Komor and Gaudelli unit is appropriate, and how to treat the parallel Nishida-Kondo (Target-AID) editor. Chabes and Somfai now name Liu alone; Chabes says he has not independently checked priority between the cytosine base editor and Target-AID papers.
B057 is attributed to Buchwald and Hartwig in Somfai's configuration; Kosugi appears on the credited list but in no configuration.
maturity_disputes: Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes the PROTAC arm premature. All six B014 supporters raise it; Zou says a few years' wait would carry little cost. Linke and Zou note that glue-class drugs are already approved.
Whether base editing's short clinical record and long-term safety data matter for timing (Chabes, Somfai, Sparr), and whether it has clearer therapeutic outcomes than degraders (Sparr).
Whether B057 is mature but incremental (Somfai) and whether B025 is mature but outside the committee's centre of gravity (Brzezinski).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member reports a conflict that requires recusal for the candidates in their configurations. Disclosed proximity only: Brzezinski's research on proton and electron transfer in cytochrome c oxidase is close to B025; Aqvist notes that B030 (Car-Parrinello) is in his own field of biomolecular simulation and says his Warshel link concerns EVB and the 2013 prize, not this method; Chabes works on DNA repair adjacent to base editing; Linke, a nanophysicist, notes that nanopore sequencing (B048) is close to his device interests; Sparr works in a general sense in the area of B021 and B045.
Institutional ties disclosed with no candidate involved: Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm University colleagues.
questions_for_round2: Can a single citation be worded so that it states the principle (small-molecule recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove a protein) and covers both PROTACs and molecular glues, and if it can, which of Ciulli or Handa is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies? Each Ciulli and Handa supporter should state what that person discovered that is not implied by the others.

If the committee chooses a PROTAC-only citation, how should the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism and the names Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray be treated, and is a PROTAC prize now defensible without an approved heterobifunctional degrader?

Is B014 alone sufficient, or should a second part be added? Chabes pairs it with B042 for Liu, and Somfai's two-part prize omits B014. Would the committee accept two chemical-biology parts in one year?
For B042, is Liu alone the defensible attribution, or should Komor and Gaudelli be included, and how should the Nishida-Kondo work and the 2020 CRISPR prize affect priority and distinctness?

What new capability do B057 and B025 add beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Marcus theory, and would their supporters (Somfai, Brzezinski) accept B014 as the main part or keep a separate part for their candidate?
summary.chair_observation: B014 has the widest explicit support (six of eight, with a majority threshold of five), but the six do not yet share a laureate set or a citation: three name Ciulli, two name Handa, and one names Crews and Deshaies alone. Support for the other candidates is one or two members each. Round 2 therefore turns on the third laureate and the PROTAC and glue scope of the citation, whether a second part is wanted, and how much weight the lack of an approved PROTAC should carry.
